verdict.rationale: The evidence shows iTerm2's shell integration can work 'even over ssh', but it depends on a login script installed on each remote host, with triggers offered as a fallback. That is a manual per-host arrangement, not a terminal-owned SSH integration that carries terminfo, shell integration and config to the remote. Hostname-based profile switching and tmux -CC are adjacent features that do not transfer anything to the remote host, so no credit is given.

support.subject: As a developer, I can SSH to remote hosts with the terminal's own integration carrying my terminfo, shell integration, and config along
